question: Which of the following perennial rivers is 720 km long and originates in the Himalayas in flow through chamba of Himachal Pradesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi river.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ravi river** originates in the **Himalayas **and flows through **Chamba district** of Himachal Pradesh, before **entering Punjab** and finally joining the **Chenab river.**
 
• **Saryu river** is a tributary of the **Ghaghara river** and flows through **Uttar Pradesh and Nepal.**
 
• **Yamuna river **is a major tributary of the Ganga river and originates in the** Yamunotri glacier** in the Himalayas.
 
 
• It flows through several states, including **Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Delhi**, before merging with the Ganga at **Allahabad.**
 
 
 
• **Krishna river** is a major river in South India and originates in the **Western Ghats of Maharashtra**.
 
 
• It flows through several states, including **Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh,** before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Ravi river **is an important river in **North India and Pakistan**, with a total length of about **720 km.**
 
• It is a **transboundary river,** meaning it flows through both **India and Pakistan**.
 
• The river has several major tributaries, including the **Bhadal and Tant Gari **rivers in Himachal Pradesh, and the** Ujh and Beas r**ivers in Punjab.
 
• The Ravi river has been dammed at several places, including the** Chamera Dam in Himachal Pradesh, and the Ranjit Sagar Dam in Punjab.**
 
• These dams provide **hydroelectric power and irrigation water** to the surrounding areas.
 
• The Ravi river basin is home to several important wildlife species, including the **Himalayan black bear, snow leopard, and musk deer.**
 
• The river is also an important **source of fish** for the local communities.
